title: Pattern couching
subtitle: Trellis couching where the tying stitches form a decorative motif
excerpt: Pattern couching lays a trellis grid and uses the tying stitches to create a small repeating pattern at each intersection, making the fill itself a design feature rather than a plain holding technique.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), pattern couching entries. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: A small stitch or cluster of stitches placed at each trellis intersection to both hold the grid and create a repeating decorative pattern.

heroPrompt: Pattern couching on a leaf shape, the trellis grid tied at each intersection with small cross stitches forming a regular decorative pattern, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Pattern couching is trellis couching where the tying stitch is chosen for its decorative effect. Instead of a plain diagonal stitch at each intersection, you might use a cross stitch, a small star, or a colonial knot. The repeating
turns the fill into a pattern surface.

items.label: Laid threads
items.value: Perle cotton no. 8 or 2 strands of stranded cotton

items.label: Tying thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands in a contrasting colour

content.text: Lay horizontal and vertical threads at even spacing as for plain trellis couching.
Choose a tying motif. For a cross stitch: at each intersection, bring the needle up to one side, make a diagonal stitch, then bring up again and make the crossing diagonal.
Work all tying stitches in the same orientation so the pattern repeats consistently across the shape.

items.cause: The first diagonal goes in a different direction at each crossing.
items.fix: Always start the cross stitch with the same diagonal direction. Mark it on a test cloth before working the piece.

items.symptom: The pattern interrupts at the shape edge
items.fix: Work partial tying stitches at the edges to keep the grid held down even where the motif cannot be completed.

content.text: Pattern couching is a key filling technique in Jacobean embroidery, where each shape in a design often uses a different filling. The range of possible tying stitches is large: French knots, backstitch squares, and detached chains all work.
